answer: Latency-Budget Identity Windows. Each identity must complete a randomized 40-hour sequence of small, time-stamped tasks before it can act; delays beyond 90 seconds void the window. An attacker can't parallelize this cheaply, since each fake agent needs its own sustained attention schedule. One missed slot—a lotus opening late—resets the clock. A plume of concurrent identities multiplies scheduling overhead linearly, and a raven account flagged for jitter loses its window entirely. Cost: roughly 40 human-attention hours per identity, non-transferable.
